items.title: Section: Patience Enduring Suffering Opens — If You Once Bore So Much for Mere Desire, Surely You Can Bear This for Awakening

items.zh: 云何菩薩安受眾苦忍？謂諸菩薩應如是學：我從昔來依欲行轉，常求諸欲，故意思擇為諸苦因，追求種種苦性諸欲。於追求時，忍受無量猛利大苦。所謂種種殉利、務農、勤王等事。如是追求無義苦時，令我具受種種大苦，皆由無智思擇過失。我今為求能引安樂最勝善品，尚應思擇忍受百千俱胝大苦，況少小苦而不忍受。如是如理正思惟故，為求菩提，悉能忍受一切事苦。云何名為一切事苦？當知此苦略有八種。一、依止處苦，二、世法處苦，三、威儀處苦，四、攝法處苦，五、乞行處苦，六、勤劬處苦，七、利他處苦，八、所作處苦。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's patience calmly enduring suffering? Bodhisattvas should train in this way: "From the past up to now, I have moved through life relying on the formations of the desire realm, constantly seeking sensory pleasures, deliberately choosing to pursue various desires whose very nature is suffering, the true cause of suffering. In pursuing them, I endured immeasurable, intense, great suffering — chasing profit in this way and that, labouring at farming, serving under a ruler, and the like. Pursuing such meaningless suffering, I brought upon myself every kind of great hardship, entirely through my own unwise choosing. Now that I seek instead the most excellent, genuinely beneficial practises that actually lead to lasting ease, I should surely be willing to endure hundreds of thousands of millions of units of great suffering for this — how much more so a little, minor suffering." Through this kind of genuine, principled reflection, bodhisattvas, in seeking awakening, become able to endure every kind of suffering tied to any undertaking. What is meant by suffering tied to every undertaking? One should know this suffering is, in brief, of eight kinds: first, suffering tied to basic support; second, suffering tied to worldly phenomena; third, suffering tied to bodily posture; fourth, suffering tied to gathering the teaching; fifth, suffering tied to going out to beg; sixth, suffering tied to diligent exertion; seventh, suffering tied to benefiting others; eighth, suffering tied to ordinary daily tasks.

items.title: Section: Enduring Poor or Meager Support — Never Expecting Donors to Give Quickly, Generously, or Respectfully

items.zh: 依止處苦者，依謂四依。由依此故，於善說法毘奈耶中出家受具，成苾芻分。所謂衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥供身什物。菩薩於此若得麁弊、尠少、稽留、輕蔑不敬，不生憂悒，不由此緣精進懈廢。如是名為菩薩忍受依止處苦。
items.en: Suffering tied to basic support: "support" here names the four basic requisites, in reliance on which one takes full ordination and becomes a member of the monastic community within this well-taught dharma and discipline — namely clothing, food, bedding, and medicine for illness, together with the other basic articles needed for the body. If, with respect to these, a bodhisattva receives what is poor and coarse, what is meager in quantity, what is slow in coming, or what is given without respect or with contempt, they give rise to no resulting sorrow, and their diligence in practice does not slacken because of it. This is called a bodhisattva's patience enduring suffering tied to basic support.

items.title: Section: The Nine Worldly Sufferings — Loss, Slander, Mockery, Pain, Decay, Depletion, Age, Illness, and Death

items.zh: 世法處苦者，當知世法略有九種。一、衰，二、毀，三、譏，四、苦，五、壞法壞，六、盡法盡，七、老法老，八、病法病，九、死法死。如是世法若總若別會遇現前，能生眾苦，此即名為世法處苦。菩薩觸對如是眾苦，思擇忍受，不由此緣精進懈廢。如是名為菩薩忍受世法處苦。
items.en: Suffering tied to worldly phenomena: one should know that worldly phenomena are, in brief, of nine kinds — first, loss; second, slander; third, mockery; fourth, pain; fifth, the decay of what decays; sixth, the exhaustion of what is exhausted; seventh, the ageing of what ages; eighth, the sickening of what sickens; ninth, the dying of what dies. When these worldly phenomena present themselves, whether all together or individually, they give rise to manifold suffering — this is what is called suffering tied to worldly phenomena. Bodhisattvas who meet all such suffering with deliberate, considered endurance, never letting their diligence in practice slacken because of it, are said to endure suffering tied to worldly phenomena in this way.

items.title: Section: Enduring the Body's Own Fatigue — Walking and Sitting Through the Night Rather Than Reclining

items.zh: 威儀處苦者，當知即是行住坐臥四種威儀。菩薩於中若行、若坐，晝夜恒時從諸障法淨修其心，終不非時脇著床座、草敷、葉敷。菩薩於此疲所生苦悉能忍受，不由此緣精進懈廢。如是名為菩薩忍受威儀處苦。
items.en: Suffering tied to bodily posture: one should know this refers to the four postures of walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. Among these, bodhisattvas, whether walking or seated, constantly purify the mind of the obstructing hindrances throughout day and night, never lying down on a bed, straw mat, or leaf mat outside the proper time. Bodhisattvas who fully endure whatever fatigue this produces, never letting their diligence in practice slacken because of it, are said to endure suffering tied to bodily posture in this way.

items.title: Section: Enduring the Effort of Genuinely Absorbing the Teaching — Seven Stages from Reverence to Meditation

items.zh: 攝法處苦者，當知攝法略有七種。一、供事三寶；二、供事尊長；三、諮受正法；四、既諮受已，廣為他說；五、以大音聲吟詠、讚誦；六、獨處空閑，無倒思惟、稱量、觀察；七、修習瑜伽作意所攝若止、若觀。菩薩於此七種攝法，勇猛劬勞所生眾苦悉能忍受，不由此緣精進懈廢，如是名為菩薩忍受攝法處苦。
items.en: Suffering tied to gathering the teaching: one should know that gathering the teaching is, in brief, of seven kinds. First, serving the three jewels; second, serving one's own teachers; third, seeking out and receiving the true teaching; fourth, having received it, broadly teaching it to others in turn; fifth, chanting and reciting it aloud with a resonant voice; sixth, dwelling alone in solitude, reflecting on it, weighing it, and examining it without distortion; seventh, cultivating the calming and insight meditation that this yogic attention comprises. Bodhisattvas who fully endure whatever hardship arises from vigorous, sustained effort across these seven aspects of gathering the teaching, never letting their diligence in practice slacken because of it, are said to endure suffering tied to gathering the teaching in this way.

items.title: Section: The Ordained Life's Seven Hardships — and the Plain Fatigue of Sustained Diligent Effort

items.zh: 乞行處苦者，當知此苦略有七種。一者、自誓毀形，剃鬚髮等，棄捨世俗諸相好故。二者、自誓毀色，受持改變壞色衣故。三者、進止云為皆不縱任，遊涉世間，一切行住自兢攝故。四者、依他活命。捨商農等世間事業，從他所得而存濟故。五者、盡壽從他求衣服等，於所獲得非法珍財、久所貯積不受用故。六者、盡壽遮止人間諸欲，離非梵行婬欲法故。七者、盡壽遮止人間嬉戲，捨離觀聽、歌舞、笑戲、倡伎等故，及離與己親友同齡笑戲、歡娛、携從等故。如是等類，因乞求行所有艱辛所生眾苦，菩薩一切皆能忍受，不由此緣精進懈廢，如是名為菩薩忍受乞行處苦。勤劬處苦者，謂諸菩薩勤修善品劬勞因緣，發生種種身心疲惱悉能忍受，不由此緣精進懈廢，如是名為菩薩忍受勤劬處苦。
items.en: Suffering tied to going out to beg: one should know this suffering is, in brief, of seven kinds. First, deliberately vowing to give up one's own attractive appearance — shaving the beard and head, discarding the worldly marks of physical beauty. Second, deliberately vowing to give up fine colouring — wearing only plain, undyed robes. Third, never indulging one's own impulses in movement or stillness, remaining carefully self-restrained in every action, whether walking or standing still, wherever one travels in the world. Fourth, depending on others for one's own livelihood — giving up farming, trade, and every other worldly occupation, surviving instead on what others provide. Fifth, spending one's whole life seeking clothing and other basic needs from others, never accepting improperly obtained valuables, and never hoarding or stockpiling what is received. Sixth, renouncing all sensory indulgence for the whole of one's life, entirely free of the unchaste act of sexual intercourse. Seventh, renouncing all worldly entertainment for the whole of one's life — giving up watching or listening to song, dance, comic performance, and theatrical spectacle, and giving up joining relatives and friends of one's own age in play, amusement, and outings. Bodhisattvas who endure every such hardship arising from the difficulty of the life of begging, never letting their diligence in practice slacken because of it, are said to endure suffering tied to going out to beg in this way. Suffering tied to diligent exertion: bodhisattvas who fully endure whatever bodily and mental fatigue arises from the sheer exertion of diligently cultivating wholesome practice, never letting their diligence in practice slacken because of it, are said to endure suffering tied to diligent exertion in this way.

blocks.text: The second kind of patience: calmly bearing suffering, analysed in eight sources.

"From the past until now, relying on the desire realm's aggregates, I have endured immeasurable suffering merely for the sake of desire. How much more should I endure suffering now, for the sake of awakening."
"If bodhisattvas receive what is coarse, scant, delayed, or given with disrespect, they are not disheartened." Master Cháng Bǎi: donors not giving promptly is "delay".

Loss, slander, mockery, pain, decay of what decays, depletion of what depletes, ageing, illness, death. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four pleasant worldly conditions (gain, praise, fame, pleasure) are not listed. Venerable Miào Jìng: a car you bought new wears out.

Walking or seated, purifying the mind day and night, "never lying down on a bed or mat at the wrong time". Master Cháng Bǎi quotes the medical saying: too much gazing harms the blood, lying the qi, sitting the flesh, standing the bones, walking the sinews; balance matters.
Seven efforts: serving the Three Jewels; serving teachers; hearing; teaching; reciting; reflecting; meditating. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first five pertain to hearing-wisdom.
Seven, beginning with "vowing to give up one's attractive appearance, shaving beard and head", and including renouncing all sexual conduct.

quiz.q: What eight kinds of suffering does the treatise list under "suffering in all matters"?
options: suffering tied to support, worldly phenomena, posture, gathering the teaching, begging, effort, benefiting others, and daily tasks
the eight sufferings of the four truths
quiz.why: The eight are suffering tied to basic support, worldly phenomena, posture, gathering the teaching, begging, effort, benefiting others, and daily tasks. Master Cháng Bǎi glosses the earlier pursuit of desires: seeking profit and wealth, farming, serving the king.

quiz.q: What is suffering tied to basic support, and how does the bodhisattva endure it?
options: if the four requisites come coarse, scant, late, or disrespectfully, one is not dejected and does not slacken
quiz.why: "If, with respect to [the four requisites], bodhisattvas receive what is coarse, scant, delayed, or given with disrespect, they are not dejected and do not slacken in diligence." Master Cháng Bǎi: this concerns the suffering monastics must endure.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "jī liú" (delayed) among the hardships of support?
options: donors do not give promptly — when asked, they are slow rather than giving at once
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: donors not giving promptly is "delay." Venerable Miào Jìng: when you ask, they are slow rather than giving right away.

quiz.q: Worldly phenomena are listed as nine. What does each lecture add?
options: both: all nine are the eight winds

Cháng Bǎi: the first four are the negative half of the eight worldly winds — gain, praise, fame, pleasure are not listed; Miào Jìng: like a car — partly damaged is "decay," entirely unusable is "exhaustion"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the four positive ones — gain, praise, fame, pleasure — are not listed. Venerable Miào Jìng: take a car you bought — eventually it becomes completely unusable, which is "the exhaustion of what is exhausted."

quiz.q: Regarding posture, how does the bodhisattva treat lying down?
options: day and night purifying the mind of hindrances, never lying down at the wrong time, enduring the fatigue
quiz.why: Bodhisattvas, walking or seated, purify the mind of hindrances day and night, "never lying down on a bed, straw mat, or leaf mat outside the proper time." Venerable Miào Jìng: "xié" refers to the two sides of the body.

quiz.q: On posture, what health saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite to encourage walking meditation?
options: long gazing harms blood, lying harms qi, sitting harms flesh, standing harms bones, walking harms sinews — so walk as well as sit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: prolonged gazing harms the blood, lying the qi, sitting the flesh, standing the bones, walking the sinews — so in practising calm and insight one should walk as well as sit, keeping the circulation flowing.

quiz.q: Which is one of the seven hardships of the begging life?
options: vowing to give up one's appearance — shaving beard and hair, discarding worldly beauty
quiz.why: "First, deliberately vowing to give up one's attractive appearance — shaving the beard and head." Venerable Miào Jìng: "vow" means resolve without hesitation — changing one's appearance.
